task: Describe and compare source-backed experimental transformations in published genomics sequencing assays, in a graph usable for future protocol design.
observable_inputs: Exact published workflow and source packet versions
Explicit selected operations and their material/data connections
Source passages and actual inspected Methods/supplements
Existing admitted transformation definitions when retrieving known components
scientific_object: A correspondence at a declared level of mechanistic resolution; not an unqualified claim of biochemical equivalence or experimentally demonstrated transfer.
invariants: Renaming operations or moving module boundaries must not by itself change a scientific judgment.
Splitting one source-described transformation into several graph operations may change representation but not its molecular input/output and information consequences.
Preserve physical material versus computational data, native analyte versus read molecule, chemical mark versus readout, and observed versus inferred identities.
Unknown evidence is not a wildcard match; missing a match or proof is not evidence of incompatibility.
A shared transformation does not establish shared assay architecture, historical ancestry or contextual substitutability.
alternatives_to_audit: Broad purpose grouping versus mechanism-specific grouping versus implementation-specific equivalence
One-to-one operations versus connected groups with preserved internal interfaces
Fixed universal workflow steps versus common comparison questions plus scoped mechanism-specific required properties
Machine check of explicit rule coverage versus LLM or expert scientific interpretation of evidence
required_outputs: Plain-language rule with scientific rationale and exact source links
Critical compared properties, applicability and expected evidence
Rule outcomes: supported agreement, supported difference, unresolved, not_applicable with reason
Explicit context-transfer unknowns kept distinct from established incompatibility
Source-backed positive, hard-negative and unknown test cases; no forced edges
success_checks: Source facts recorded separately from locally designed comparison rules
Whole-scope mechanism claims cover consequential transformations, including claimed information changes
Different reaction chemistries yielding the same sequencing signal are not merged as the same chemical mechanism
Same mechanism in changed substrate/support/context retains those differences and does not imply demonstrated compatibility
Direct RNA and non-amplifying workflows do not require fictional cDNA/PCR steps
Code enforces required checks, binding and nonpromotion of unresolved cases; scientific judgment itself remains fallible
negative_controls: Same word or enzyme, different transformation
Same T-to-C readout, different label-conversion chemistry
Cell/spatial barcode versus bulk sample index
Hybridization association versus covalent information attachment
Native RNA readout versus sequencing a DNA copy
Purely structural group connectivity without common biochemical transformation
scope_limit: Representative primary-source audit and software rules, not complete coverage of all methods, expert certification or wet-lab feasibility validation. No new native model extraction jobs are launched locally.
